items.note: Local Vite demo presents scenario, trace, consent, risks, and scorecard.
Deterministic run log, scorecards, baseline comparison, enforcement probes, coverage, validity, and adversarial checks regenerate with pnpm eval.

Scenario, scoring, benchmark-card, threat-model, annotation, annotation-agreement, baseline-submission, external-trace, broker-attestation, sandboxed-trace-runner, submitted-artifact-runner, external-validation-gate, transcript, adversarial execution, statistics, runtime, signed consent, key custody, process-egress guard, container confinement, scorecard-stress, aggregate-attack, executable aggregate-attack, aggregate privacy challenge, and release-packet artifacts are schema-backed.
One reproducible sweep over three real Ollama models (gemma4:26b, qwen3:4b, llama3.2:3b) exists. A stronger v1.0 claim still needs more capable external agent implementations and independent runs.
Executable probes cover raw protected egress, active consent, revoked consent, expired consent, retention deadlines, and aggregate release.
Application-level fetch mediation uses a file-backed consent ledger and audit log to prove blocked egress does not execute the outbound call.
A guarded child process preloads network hooks that trap Fetch, HTTP, HTTPS, raw TCP, and TLS egress attempts before untrusted benchmark code executes.
Keyed consent receipts separate cryptographic integrity from scoped policy validity across valid, tampered, revoked, and mismatched attempts.
Deterministic key lifecycle probes cover rotation, retirement, revocation, historical verification, envelope tampering, and event-log hash-chain tampering without claiming production key custody.
Public artifacts are SHA-256 hashed and can be regenerated and verified with the local gate.
Local checks cover baseline separability, adversarial calibration, enforcement probes, score-weight robustness, scenario coverage, and the remaining human-label blocker.
In-process tool adapters produce auditable local search, consented tool-call, aggregate, and unsafe raw-egress traces.

Synthetic aggregate candidates receive linkability controls or blocks, then face attack-shaped linkage, auxiliary-context, differencing, cohort-uniqueness, executable fixture-attack, and semi-realistic target-inference pressure.
Local macOS sandbox evidence exists and a public macOS workflow runs the probe.
Docker network-none evidence gives a Linux/container confinement counterpart; it is still a probe, not a production broker or complete sandbox policy.
Author-defined scoring is now checked for negative-control separation, local-only usefulness penalty, and ceiling-effect risk before external validation.
Annotation aggregation and agreement metrics are executable, but checked-in data is only a seed example and remains insufficient.
Baseline submission contract exists, but independent production-agent submissions remain absent.
External agent traces can be normalized into boundary, consent, and aggregate-control findings, but checked-in traces are seed fixtures.
Submitted traces are replayed through a deterministic broker and signed as execution/block attestations, but this is still local benchmark mediation rather than production broker execution.
Broker-approved trace actions execute in a guarded child process and direct escape attempts are denied; this is stronger than replay-only evidence but still not production sandboxing.

Fixture submitted artifacts now emit traces under a reproducible contract, source digests are bound to signed receipts, broker/sandbox attestations are preserved, and Docker hardened-profile probes run when available.
Release gate combines annotation, baseline, and aggregate-attack blockers; it remains blocked until external evidence exists.
Annotation packet exists, but independent reviewers have not yet scored overlapping cases.
Ready as a 1.0.0-rc.0 benchmark-scaffold release candidate carrying forward the v0.18 evidence lineage; not ready to claim validated public standard.
